subject.title: chore(deps-dev): bump the development-minor-and-patch group across 1 directory with 13 updates

question: Should this dependency bundle keep the `@react-email/ui@6.6.6` and `vite@8.1.3` updates despite Socket's obfuscated-code warnings, or should those updates be split or held?
rationale: Automation can repair the formatter output, but it should not decide whether new obfuscated-code supply-chain warnings in build/test tooling are acceptable risk.

options.title: Hold flagged updates
options.body: Drop or split the `@react-email/ui` and Vite updates that introduced Socket alerts, keep the safer dependency bumps, and include the `oxfmt` formatting output.

options.title: Accept after secops review
options.body: Keep the full bundle only if the security owner accepts the Socket warnings and the formatter failure is fixed before merge.

options.title: Wait for a cleaner bundle
options.body: Close or pause this grouped PR and let Dependabot regenerate smaller updates if splitting the flagged packages is cleaner than repairing this branch.

recommendation.title: Hold flagged updates
recommendation.body: Drop or split the `@react-email/ui` and Vite updates that introduced Socket alerts, keep the safer dependency bumps, and include the `oxfmt` formatting output.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is whether the new Socket obfuscation alerts are acceptable supply-chain risk.
